title: ci: use 16-core GitHub runners
body:
## Summary
- move Ubuntu GitHub Actions jobs from `ubuntu-latest` to the org hosted `ubuntu-24.04-16core` runner
- keep workflow logic unchanged; this only changes runner capacity

## Motivation
Reduce CI/build lead time across Divine repos. The org runner `ubuntu-24.04-16core` is configured as Ubuntu 24.04, 16 cores, 64 GB RAM, max 50 concurrent runners.

## Manual validation
- Parsed changed workflow YAML with Ruby
- Ran `git diff --check -- .github/workflows`

title: fix: HLS.js fallback for video playback in media preview
body:
## Summary

- some uploaded videos fail to play in Chrome's native `<video>` decoder. divine-web already handles this with HLS.js fallback to transcoded segments — the admin UI didn't have it.
- adds `HlsVideo` component: tries native MP4 first, falls back to HLS.js (transcoded segments via `VITE_CDN_DOMAIN`), then to the authenticated media proxy for gated content
- distinguishes "content not available" (404/deleted) from "failed to load" (other errors) in the media preview UI
- fixes the `showByDefault` race condition where media would flash-show then collapse as report priority data loaded (tri-state `hasHighPriorityReports`)
- adds `blob:` to `media-src` CSP in worker fallback HTML to match dev CSP
- shows full sha256 hashes in media preview (no truncation)

## Test plan

- [x] open a report with video content at relay.admin.divine.video — videos that previously showed as black rectangles with inactive controls should now play via HLS
- [x] open a report with image content — images still load normally
- [x] open a report with a high-priority category — media should start hidden
- [x] open a report with a non-high-priority category — media should start visible
- [x] verify no CORS errors in browser console on report list or report detail pages
- [x] verify deleted/unavailable media shows "Content not available" (ImageOff icon) instead of generic warning triangle

Verified on staging worker and test frontend deployment.

title: feat: age review clock — 15-day under-16 moderation workflow
body:
## Summary

- D1 schema (`age_review_cases` + `account_notes`) with migration + runtime fallback
- ReportWatcher auto-creates case when `NS-underageUser` report arrives
- Admin API: CRUD for cases and account notes (behind CF Access / API key auth)
- Mobile-facing `/v1/` endpoints with NIP-98 user auth (matches divine-mobile PR #3531 contract)
- Cron deadline checker: Slack alerts for approaching deadlines, auto-close on expiry
- Admin UI: Age Review tab with split-pane queue, case detail panel, moderator actions (state transitions, clock pause/resume, age band change, clear/deny), account notes

## Context

Backend for the 15-day age review clock described in the under-16 system coordination doc (support-trust-safety `working-draft`). divine-mobile PR #3531 defines the client-side flow and API contract this PR implements.

Mobile app calls `/v1/account/moderation-status` to check if the authenticated user is under review, and `/v1/minor-review-cases/:caseId/parent-contact` to submit parent email. Both use NIP-98 (kind 27235) auth — the app already signs all backend requests via `Nip98AuthService`.

## New env var

- `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` (optional) — Slack incoming webhook for deadline alerts

## Test plan

- [ ] Apply migration on staging: `wrangler d1 migrations apply`
- [ ] Send test `NS-underageUser` report on staging relay, verify case row created
- [ ] Verify admin API: list/get/update cases via curl with X-Admin-Key
- [ ] Verify `/v1/account/moderation-status` with NIP-98 signed request
- [ ] Verify admin UI: Age Review tab loads, case list, detail panel, state transitions
- [ ] Set test case deadline to near-expiry, trigger cron, verify Slack alert
- [ ] Verify clock pause/resume math preserves remaining days correctly

title: Age review: Zendesk integration for parent contact workflow
body:
## Context

PR #67 adds the age review clock — 15-day case management for under-16 reports. When a flagged user submits their parent's email via the mobile app, the email is saved to the case and the clock pauses. Currently, the moderator sees the email in the admin UI and handles outreach manually.

This issue adds Zendesk automation so parent contact is tracked as a ticket with proper threading, SLA, and reply detection.

## Scope

### Outbound: auto-create Zendesk ticket on parent email submission

When `POST /v1/minor-review-cases/{caseId}/parent-contact` saves the parent email:

- Create a Zendesk ticket addressed to the parent email
- Template body explains the situation, asks parent to reply to verify
- Tag the ticket `age-review` + include case ID in a custom field or internal note
- Use existing Zendesk API patterns from `worker/src/index.ts` (ticket creation, custom fields)
- Non-blocking: ticket creation failure should not fail the parent-contact endpoint (log + continue)

### Inbound: webhook on parent reply

- New endpoint: `POST /api/zendesk/age-review-reply` (sits alongside existing `/api/zendesk/` routes, uses Zendesk webhook auth)
- Zendesk trigger: when a ticket tagged `age-review` receives a new reply from the requester, fire webhook
- Handler matches ticket to case (by case ID in custom field or by requester email lookup)
- Updates case: log that parent contact was received, optionally transition state to `submitted_for_review`
- Moderator still makes the final clear/deny decision

### Zendesk-side configuration

- New trigger: "Age review — parent replied" (condition: tag `age-review`, requester replied)
- Webhook target pointing at `POST /api/zendesk/age-review-reply` on the worker
- Custom field or tag convention for linking ticket to case ID
- Email template for outbound parent notification

## Dependencies

- PR #67 (age review clock) must be merged first
- `ZENDESK_API_TOKEN` and `ZENDESK_EMAIL` env vars (already available on the worker for existing Zendesk integration)

## Not in scope

- Auto-closing cases based on Zendesk ticket resolution (moderator decision stays manual)
- Parent identity verification beyond "they replied to the email"
- Multi-language email templates (English only for MVP)
